layer: Frontend and static delivery (all web surfaces and how they are served)
summary: The frontend layer is three web apps with no framework and no bundler: the Sandbox Console (the operator UI for banks, exchanges and document issuers), the Playground (free-tier anchoring, an offline bundle verifier and the public PoR inclusion page) and the Developer Hub. Each is compiled by one tsc pass into unminified ES modules and served by the core API process itself (static.ts, :8787). Beside them are the Express + cheerio marketing homepage (:3100) and three demo sites. Nothing sits in front of any of them: no TLS, no reverse proxy, no CDN and no compression. Core sends static files with Cache-Control: no-cache and no ETag or Last-Modified, so a 304 is impossible and every console reload re-downloads about 30 files (~510 KB). That happens on the same event loop that runs the transaction API and the batch and remit workers. The layer's main strength is deliberate: heavy and sensitive work stays in the browser (document hashing, PoR sum-tree building, bundle and PoR verification), so the server receives 32 bytes or one signed statement whatever the document or ledger size. Console request rate scales with the number of operators, not with transaction volume. Only the live settlement tracker (0.4 req/s per open row, up to 10 min) and the PoR anchor watch (0.5 req/s, up to 3 min) poll; nothing else auto-refreshes and row details load on click. The weakness is that the cost of each console request grows with the org's data. The home dashboard runs ~25 statements per view, about 8 of them whole-org aggregates and 13 whose results are no longer shown. Every cold load runs month-to-date COUNT(*)s twice, and the subscriptions call runs 6 more. The settlement ledger recomputes COUNT(*) on every page, and its search is LIKE '%q%' plus JSON_EXTRACT over events. The records screen has no pagination at all (newest 50; the keyed API stops at 500 with no cursor). All of these share a 10-connection MySQL pool with the transaction path, with no statement timeout. At 100k rows per org the console gets slow; at 10M rows per org the dashboard and search would take tens of seconds to minutes per view (estimate, not measured) and could starve writes. Console sign-in runs scryptSync on the event loop and stalls all core traffic for a few hundred milliseconds. The production host split described in comments cannot work as built (CSP connect-src 'self', no CORS on console routes), so a CDN must keep one origin through path routing. The demo sites are demonstrations that integrate through the published REST API and SDK and keep JSON-file state; do not count them as product, although their polling does hit the shared core.

components.name: Core static server (fallback mounts)
components.role: Serves /console/, /playground/ and /docs/ from the API process, and redirects / to /console/
components.notes: Only consulted after the linear scan of ~69 API routes misses. Live .env sets PLAYGROUND_DIR, DOCS_DIR and CONSOLE_DIR to the three dist folders. Plain HTTP on all interfaces. Cache-Control: no-cache; no ETag, Last-Modified, gzip/br, Range or Content-Length. A strict self-only CSP plus nosniff and no-referrer goes on every file. Same process as the API, BatchWorker and RemitWorker (pm2 fork, 1 instance).

components.name: Sandbox Console (apps/console)
components.role: Operator UI with 8 hash-routed sections: dashboard, settlements ledger with live tracker and manifests, PoR anchoring, anchor (digest, inscription, signed, verify), records, subscriptions/billing, integrate (keys), audit log
components.tech: TypeScript, compiled by tsc to unminified ES modules with sourcemaps; no framework or bundler; template strings + innerHTML; vendored attest-verify and portable attest-por SDK sources
components.notes: Auth is a DB-backed session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 14 days; not Secure on this box); the page stores no browser data. Korean/English via ?lang= or navigator.language. Same-origin API (meta attest-api=""). Cold load is 30 requests, ~510 KB, 4-level import waterfall. sandbox.ts is compiled but never imported. All routes are refused unless STONEHASH_ENV=test.

components.name: Playground (apps/playground)
components.role: Public pages: free-tier anchoring without signup, offline proof-bundle verifier, and the PoR end-user inclusion verifier (por.html)
components.notes: index: 17 modules, 96 KB. por.html: 18 requests, ~114 KB. Verification is offline. The anchor panel calls the CORS-enabled /v1/public/anchors. por.html fetches /v1/public/por/snapshots/:id through a root-relative (same-origin) path. The app.ts header still says 'no StoneHash endpoint is contacted', but the anchor panel now contacts one.

components.name: Developer Hub (apps/docs)
components.role: Public documentation: 11 Markdown guides (Korean for 7), OpenAPI reference rendered in the browser, SDK tarballs with checksums
components.tech: tsc ES modules (4 modules, 43 KB), own Markdown renderer
components.notes: Content is fetched per page and cached in tab memory. openapi.json is 372,899 B, uncompressed. GET /v1/meta drives the network badge. download/*.tar.gz (37-130 KB) is served by core as octet-stream.

components.name: Marketing homepage (homepage/, pm2 stonehash-homepage :3100)
components.role: Marketing and use-case pages, hash/verify demos, a hero anchor demo that calls core's free tier, and an admin page for translations and site config
components.tech: Express 5 + cheerio server-side i18n (?lang= and a lang cookie); express.static for /assets, /css, /js
components.notes: Binds 0.0.0.0 with trust proxy on; no CSP or helmet. Assets are 73 MB, including 8-17 MB autoplay videos on legacy pages. serve.json is legacy and unused by Express. README and start.sh are stale (port 3010). ATTEST_API_URL points at core :8787. Separate process from core, same box.

components.name: Demo bank (demo-bank, :3200)
components.role: Demonstration of a bank's own integration: signed anchoring through a docker attest-sign container and an openssl 'HSM', plus a remittance adapter
components.tech: node:http, vendored verifier, JSON files (data/records.json, data/remit-cases.json)
components.notes: Not on the product path. Uses only REST with a bearer key, plus a console login when subscribing. Its browser refresh fans out to core GET /v1/settlements/:id.

components.name: Demo customers portal (demo-customers, :3400)
components.role: Three customer-type tabs (document issuer, exchange PoR, bank remittance) written against the published SDKs
components.tech: node:http; imports attest-sign, attest-verify, attest-por and attest-remit package sources
components.notes: JSON books rewritten whole on every save. The browser refreshes every 2.5 s with 3 fetches, all answered from memory (no core call).

components.name: Partner simulators UI (demo-partners/public, :3300)
components.role: Dashboard for the simulated receiving side (BFI, SG payout bank, settlement entity)
components.notes: A sandbox stand-in for real counterparties. Refreshes every 2 s with 3 fetches; wallet/state calls anvil balanceOf.

components.name: Settlement-chain explorer (Otterscan + nginx :5106)
components.role: Block explorer for the anvil settlement chain (owned by the chain/infra reader)
components.tech: nginx inside a docker container, gzip_static, expires max/30d
components.notes: The only nginx on the box; it fronts nothing else. No host-level nginx, Caddy, HAProxy or Traefik.

capacity_findings.title: Console screens run whole-org aggregates on every view, on the shared 10-connection pool
capacity_findings.affects: Console dashboard, subscriptions, boot; transaction-path latency through pool contention
capacity_findings.claim: The landing dashboard issues 24-25 statements per view (plus 2 for auth). About 8 aggregate every row the org owns (status != 'confirmed', GROUP BY status, substr(created_at,1,10) = ?), and 13 compute fields the console no longer renders: the attention counts and items, signed counts, webhooks and the latest manifest. GET /v1/console/products adds 6 month-to-date COUNT(*)s awaited one after another, and 5 of the 8 screens call it. Every cold load runs the month quota COUNT twice. The only attestations index is (org_id, created_at), so counts filtered on product or status read every row in range. These queries share the 10-connection pool with the transaction path, with no statement timeout. The browser fetch has no timeout either, so an impatient reload re-issues the same aggregates while the abandoned ones keep running.
evidence: apps/core/src/http/console.ts:704 num(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM attestations WHERE org_id = ? AND status != 'confirmed'`, org),
apps/core/src/http/console.ts:709-710 `SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM attestations WHERE org_id = ? AND product = 'attest' GROUP BY status`
apps/core/src/http/console.ts:752 sumRow('substr(created_at, 1, 10) = ?', today),

apps/core/src/remit/routes.ts:131-133 anchorsBy = (product) => count('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM attestations WHERE org_id = ? AND created_at >= ? AND product = ?', ...) — called 3x, plus 2 more month counts at 144-153

apps/core/src/http/console.ts:187 "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM attestations WHERE org_id = ? AND created_at >= ? AND product = 'attest'" — quota; both /me and /attestations run it at every boot (app.ts:3776-3777)

apps/console/src/app.ts never reads dash.attention, attest.signed, remit.webhooks or manifest_latest (grep), yet console.ts:694-705 and 837-865 compute 9 attention statements, 715-720 two signed counts, 774-779 manifest + webhooks
apps/core/src/db.ts:943 connectionLimit: 10,  (waitForConnections: true; no queueLimit, no max_execution_time)
apps/console/src/api.ts:87-93 res = await fetch(`${BASE}${path}`, { method, credentials: 'include', ... }) — no AbortSignal or timeout
capacity_findings.quantification: Home view ≈ 38 reads (products 11 + dashboard 27), on top of a boot of 10 reads + 1 write. One org sending 1 tx/s holds ~2.6M rows per month, and the all-time aggregates grow without bound. At 100k rows per org a view takes roughly sub-second to seconds; at 10M rows per org each whole-org aggregate reads ~10M rows, i.e. tens of seconds per view (estimate, not measured). One dashboard Promise.all can hold 5 of the 10 pool connections.
capacity_findings.fix: Maintain per-org counters/rollups on write (org × product × status × day; month usage; settlement state buckets) and read the screens from them. Delete the 13 unused statements. Bound every window. Cache dashboard and products per org for 10-30 s. Give console reads their own small pool or a read replica with max_execution_time. Add a client fetch timeout.

capacity_findings.title: Settlement ledger recomputes COUNT(*) on every page, and search cannot use an index
capacity_findings.affects: Console 송금 ledger, search box, Load more, CSV export
capacity_findings.claim: Every ledger page, every 'Load more' and every export page recomputes COUNT(*) over the filtered set. A search term becomes UPPER(col) LIKE '%q%' on three columns plus three EXISTS sub-queries running JSON_EXTRACT(...) LIKE over remit_events; no index can serve that, and it fires after only a 300 ms debounce per keystroke. Each returned row then triggers its own attestation SELECT (N+1). The export walks up to 50 pages one after another.
evidence: apps/core/src/remit/store.ts:169-176 (UPPER(id) LIKE ? ESCAPE '!' OR UPPER(quote_id) LIKE ? ... OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM remit_events e WHERE e.payment_id = remit_payments.id AND e.type = 'PAYOUT_COMPLETED' AND UPPER(COALESCE(JSON_EXTRACT(...)))
apps/core/src/remit/store.ts:194-196 const total = ... `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM remit_payments WHERE ${where.join(' AND ')}` — runs for every page, before the cursor clause
apps/core/src/remit/routes.ts:451-452 attestation: p.attestation_id ? { id: p.attestation_id, status: (await d.svc.get(orgId, p.attestation_id))?.status ?? 'unknown' } : null,
apps/console/src/app.ts:2057-2064 debounce = setTimeout(() => { ... remitView.q = qInput.value.trim(); ... void fetchRemitPage(true) ... }, 300);
apps/console/src/app.ts:1751 const EXPORT_MAX = 5000;  app.ts:1765-1769 await api.settlements({ ...query, ...(cursor ? { cursor } : {}), limit: 100 });
capacity_findings.quantification: A page ≈ 30 statements (2 auth + COUNT + SELECT * LIMIT 26 + ≤25 N+1 + audit INSERT). A search costs O(payments × events per payment), twice (COUNT and page). Demo settlements carry 5-16 events (median 12), so 10M payments means ~120M event probes per keystroke. An export is ≤50 requests ≈ ≤5,200 reads + 50 audit writes.
capacity_findings.fix: Add an indexed identifier table or columns (payment_id, quote_id, chain_tx, UETR, instruction and end-to-end ids, bank refs) with exact or prefix match. Drop the per-page total, or compute it once per filter and cache it or make it approximate. Join attestation status into the page query. Make the export a server-side job writing to object storage.

capacity_findings.title: Records screen and the keyed list API have no pagination
capacity_findings.affects: Console 앵커링 기록 screen; GET /v1/attestations integrators
capacity_findings.claim: The records screen shows only the newest 50 attestations fetched at boot: no cursor, no search, no date filter, and no refetch on navigation. GET /v1/attestations stops at 500 with no cursor. Past 500 records, an org cannot enumerate its own records from either the console or the API.

capacity_findings.quantification: An org producing 1 tx/s passes 500 records in ~8 minutes. At 100k or 10M records, over 99.9% of history cannot be reached from the UI or the API. The query itself stays cheap (index (org_id, created_at), LIMIT 50).
capacity_findings.fix: Add keyset cursor (created_at, id), status/date filters and exact-digest lookup to both endpoints, and give the console 'Load more' the way the ledger has it.

capacity_findings.title: No TLS, reverse proxy or CDN in front of any surface
capacity_findings.affects: Every surface: console sessions, API keys in transit, browser crypto, HTTP/2
capacity_findings.claim: Every surface is plain HTTP straight to Node on all interfaces: core (HOST binds all interfaces; COOKIE_SECURE and TRUST_PROXY unset), the homepage (0.0.0.0) and the demos. As a result the session cookie is not Secure, the browser withholds crypto.subtle and the async clipboard (forcing pure-JS hashing), and there is no HTTP/2 to flatten the module waterfall. capacity_findings.title: Strength: no idle polling and no per-row fetches in the console

capacity_findings.title: Strength: strict CSP and security headers, no third-party code in the apps
capacity_findings.affects: Console, Playground, Developer Hub
capacity_findings.claim: Every page core serves carries a self-only CSP (no inline script or style, frame-ancestors 'none', form-action 'none') plus nosniff and no-referrer. scale_path: T2 (~100 tx/s; one large org adds ~8.6M rows/day), in order: (1) Edge: put a TLS-terminating proxy (nginx, Caddy or a cloud LB) in front of core and the homepage, with HTTP/2, gzip/br and HSTS. Set COOKIE_SECURE=1 and TRUST_PROXY=1 and bind Node to loopback. (2) Static off core: serve /console, /playground and /docs from the proxy or a CDN on the SAME origin, routing /v1/* to core. Same-origin is required by CSP connect-src 'self', the missing console CORS and the hard-coded PoR path. Then unset PLAYGROUND_DIR, DOCS_DIR and CONSOLE_DIR. Add ETag/304, precompressed assets and modulepreload for the 27-module graph; deploy atomically into versioned folders. (3) Console read model: replace the whole-org aggregates with counters/rollups maintained on write (org × product × status × day; month usage; settlement state buckets). Delete the 13 unused dashboard statements, cache dashboard and products per org for 10-30 s, and add a client fetch timeout. (4) Ledger: search an indexed identifier table instead of LIKE '%q%' + JSON_EXTRACT; drop or cache the per-page COUNT(*); join attestation status into the page query; turn CSV export into a server-side job. (5) Records: keyset cursor, filters and exact-digest lookup on both /v1/console/attestations and /v1/attestations. (6) Polling: give the tracker a conditional GET (ETag/304) or since_seq deltas or SSE; pause hidden tabs; cap concurrent follows; stop auditing polling reads and the boot-time records fetch. (7) Isolation: give console reads a separate pool or read replica with max_execution_time; make the pool size configurable; switch scryptSync to async scrypt. (8) Public PoR and bundles: send Cache-Control public/immutable once confirmed and serve through the CDN. (9) Homepage: cache rendered HTML per (path, lang); move media to the CDN; drop Vary: Cookie. (10) Move the demo sites off the production box. T3 (~1,000 tx/s; ~86M rows/day per large org), on top of T2: (1) Split the console/reporting API into its own service that reads a reporting store (CDC from MySQL into OLAP or pre-aggregated tables), so operator screens never touch the OLTP primary. (2) Serve identifier search and audit-log search from a dedicated index (OpenSearch or similar) fed by CDC; write audit rows asynchronously in batches into partitioned storage. (3) Replace per-tab polling with server push (an SSE/WebSocket gateway fed by the settlement event stream through pub/sub) that works across multiple instances. (4) Fingerprint static assets with content hashes at build time for immutable CDN caching; publish public PoR snapshots and proof bundles as static objects in object storage at anchor time. (5) Run exports and large lists as background jobs with signed download URLs; virtualise tables only if any screen ever renders more than ~5k rows. (6) Scale core horizontally behind the LB (sessions are already DB-backed; in-memory rate limiters need a shared store; owned by the backend reader).
open_questions: How is volume distributed across orgs (one dominant bank or exchange versus many small ones)? That decides whether the whole-org console aggregates bite at T1 or only at T2.
Will production run STONEHASH_ENV=live, where the console is disabled by code, or keep env=test as the operator console? If live, operators have no UI today.

What is the intended production topology (hostnames, CDN, TLS terminator, path vs host routing)? It exists only in comments (static.ts:7-8, console index.html:9-14); nothing in deploy/ or on the host.
What are the actual query latencies of the dashboard, products, quota and ledger search at 100k and 10M rows per org? Not measured, because this pass was read-only and could not query MySQL.
How fast is pure-JS SHA-256 in target browsers? The only figure is a code comment ('perhaps thirty times slower' than crypto.subtle); the PoR timings are also code-comment figures.
Do compliance requirements want screen polling recorded in the audit log (a 'who viewed what' trail)? Today every tracker poll writes a row, while dashboard reads are deliberately silent.
How large is a real settlement detail reply? The demo cache drops payloads and signatures, so the tracker's per-poll bytes are unknown.
Is demo-bank-java (:3500, in ecosystem.config.cjs:99-110) expected to run? It was not examined and is not in the live process list.
Is a proxy planned for the homepage (its trust proxy=true implies nginx)? Today it is exposed directly on :3100.
